subject: Deal framing: Optimize Efficiency Cookbook pilot + quantization options
messages:
From: Emma Park <emma@clearstream.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging options and pilot credits for Optimize toolkit

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the Optimize toolkit looks promising for our alerting and triage pipelines. Procurement asked me to get a clearer run-down of the packaging options you mentioned (pilot credits, commit tiers, and any technical constraints when we apply aggressive quantization/batching).

Two specific asks from my side:
- Can you summarize 2–3 pilot packaging options with expected token savings and a rough credit/discount expectation?
- For our use case (short chat prompts + long retrieval context, avg seq 512), what are the practical limits and quality trade-offs between int8 quantization and fp16 when combined with KV caching and batching?

If you can send a short pricing sketch and a technical note we can share with procurement, I’ll follow up with proposed dates for an ops call next week.

Best,
Emma
Emma Park
Head of Platform
Clearstream AI

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Park <emma@clearstream.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options and pilot credits for Optimize toolkit

Hi Emma — great to meet you yesterday. Replied inline below and attached a short scenarios workbook (optimize_credit_scenarios.xlsx) with numbers you can play with. Summary first:

High-level packaging sketches (pilot-friendly):
1) Exploratory pilot (30 days) — "Cache-First"
   - Includes 200k token credits, on-hosted tier, access to Optimize dashboard + 1 week of onboarding.
   - Target: surface 30–45% token reduction via prefix/KV cache and request routing.
   - Pricing: nominal pilot credit (no cash commitment).
2) Performance pilot (60 days) — "Throughput"
   - 600k token credits, reserved slot for peak windows, 2 days of runtime tuning.
   - Target: 40–60% effective savings combining batching + model variant routing.
   - Pricing: small one-time pilot fee to reserve capacity.
3) Efficiency pilot (90 days) — "Aggressive quant + cache"
   - 1.5M token credits, quantization consultation + quality regression monitoring.
   - Target: 50–70% unit-cost reduction (depends on regen rates).
   - Pricing: credits + 3% service surcharge for active regression tracking.

Key technical notes for your avg seq=512 workload:
- Batching: returns biggest wins for throughput. If request latency SLO is loose (>=300ms), we can batch more aggressively and push unit-cost down. If sub-100ms, batching gains shrink.
- KV caching: prefix reuse from retrieval will often yield 20–40% token savings for stable prompts. Important to instrument prompt fingerprinting to avoid cache misses.
- Quantization: int8 gives material CPU/GPU memory benefits and often 1.5–2x speedups in the runtime, but quality drift appears for generative completions with long context if you aggressively quantize both weights and KV caches. We recommend int8 for reranking/embeddings/short-completion paths and fp16 or hybrid for long-context generation unless you accept a ~3–6% LLM-quality delta.

I attached the scenarios workbook and a one-page quant guidance (quant_guidance_v1.pdf). Would you and procurement be available for a 30–45 minute ops + procurement sync on Wed or Thu next week?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Sales Director, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachment: optimize_credit_scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet with sample credit consumption, commit tier bands, and expected cost per 10k tokens)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Park <emma@clearstream.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options and pilot credits for Optimize toolkit

Emma — quick technical addendum from runtime/ops:

On quantization + cache interplay (practical guidance):
- KV cache representation: we recommend storing KV as fp16 in long-context paths, even when model weights run in int8. Converting KV on-the-fly can add ~5–15ms per request but avoids cumulative generative degradation.
- A/B approach: run parallel model variants (fp16 baseline + int8 candidate) behind the same routing key. Redwood's rollouts support token-level diffing and quality regression alerts tied to your eval set; this lets you measure end-to-end user-visible delta.
- Batching knob: set a soft latency cap (p90) per route. For chat where p90 <=200ms, set batching window to 12–20ms and max batch size small; for p90 >=400ms you can expand window to 40–80ms and observe ~20–35% token-cost reduction.

If you want, we can provision a short run with your eval prompts (bring-your-own prompt set) and produce a side-by-side perf/quality report. That report is helpful for procurement to justify commit vs credits.

- Markus (Principal Product Engineer)

From: Emma Park <emma@clearstream.ai>

Thanks Lauren and Markus — this is great, exactly the kind of framing Procurement needed. A couple of follow-ups:

- Procurement wants explicit examples of expected latency and cost for two scenarios: (A) baseline fp16 with KV + light batching, (B) int8 hybrid with aggressive KV and expanded batching. Can you provide a simple table or sample numbers (p50/p90 latency, tokens/sec, estimated $/10k tokens after savings) we can drop into the SOW?
- We are very interested in the A/B run: we can share an eval bundle of ~2k representative prompts (anonymized). What are the data handling guarantees for that material during evaluation?
- Timeline: procurement expects a PO within 3–4 weeks if the pilot economics check out; are you able to hold the pilot prices for that window?

Happy to meet Thu 2027-06-03 09:00 PT for the ops + procurement call if that works for you — I’ll have procurement on the call.

Best,
Emma

2) A/B run: happy to do the eval. We will:
   - Sign an evaluation NDA / limited-data processing addendum for your prompt bundle.
   - Run both variants on your 2k anonymized prompts in a fenced environment; generate a perf + quality diff report.

3) Pricing hold: we can hold the pilot pricing sketches for 30 days from proposal date (deal_id CLR-2027-0529-OPT). If Procurement needs longer, we can extend on request but may require a short price recheck.

4) Call: Thu 2027-06-03 09:00 PT works — adding Stephanie (ops lead) and Markus (runtime) for the technical portion. I’ll send a calendar invite and include the sample numbers in advance.

Action items: Lauren to send comparative table + SOW snippet; Markus to draft evaluation addendum and runbook; Procurement to share anonymized eval prompts and preferred PO timing.

Thanks all — looking forward to the call.

Lauren Bishop

Redwood Inference
